title: Enceinte
html_source:
Pregnant in a genteel way.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: Is enceinte a ‘genteel’ way to refer to pregnancy, or is the pregnancy itself somehow genteel?

Enceinte is also just French for ‘pregnant’.

The relatively famous final sentence of the first part of Flaubert’s Madame Bovary:

Quand on partit de Tostes, au mois de mars, madame Bovary était enceinte.

‘When they left Tostes, in the month of March, Madame Bovary was pregnant.’

I don’t think Joyce was ever very into Flaubert, though.
